# git: alias: unified abort command

Add a `git abort` that runs whichever `--abort` applies to the repository's state:

```bash
$ git abort
# instead of
# git merge --abort
# git rebase --abort
# git cherry-pick --abort
```

**Motivation:** developer experience — the operation in progress is visible in `.git` (`MERGE_HEAD`, `rebase-merge/` or `rebase-apply/`, `CHERRY_PICK_HEAD`, `REVERT_HEAD`), so the alias can dispatch without the user remembering which command started it. The twin `git continue` was closed unbuilt in [[DOT-60]].
